# Hawkish Fed bets and hot US CPI keep the dollar bid; risk-off tone persists on Hormuz tensions — EUR/USD, Gold, GBP/USD, USD/JPY outlook, 11 Nov 2026 08:00 UTC

- Hawkish Fed bets and hot US CPI keep the dollar bid; risk-off tone persists on Hormuz tensions.
- Gold and silver rebounds face resistance at 4066 and 53.0; both lean lower into the window.
- USD/JPY overbought near 158.96, so the view is neutral with a sideways expectation.

The market opens the 5-hour window under pressure from a hawkish US rate repricing. Hot October CPI, with core and headline inflation above forecast, combined with Fed commentary from several officials and Goldman's call for two hikes, has pushed Treasury yields and the dollar higher. Overall sentiment is risk-off, with the Strait of Hormuz mine incident and US-Iran tensions keeping oil near 92 dollars and risk premia elevated.

The dollar is the dominant driver. Hawkish Fed bets support USD across the board, and the pause in the dollar's advance overnight looks like a consolidation rather than a reversal. Euro-zone data, including in-line German CPI, offers no counterweight, so EUR/USD remains heavy near 1.1156 and below its 4-hour EMA. Cable is also under pressure beneath its 4-hour EMA at 1.3372, with the 1.3300 area as the next reference.
